title: Wake, command, silence, task, back to listening
scenario: 'Hey Neko' then 1.5 s of speech and 1.2 s of silence (synthetic frames, fake ASR returns 'open notepad').
expected: Exactly one task 'open notepad' submitted; state back to wake_listening; the words are not kept in the outcome.

title: Every cancel phrase cancels
scenario: Commands 'cancel', 'never mind', 'forget it', 'nothing', 'no thanks', 'quiet'.
expected: No task for any of them; one cancellation each.

title: 'Stop' while a task runs stops it
scenario: A task is running and the command is 'stop'.
expected: stop() called once; nothing submitted.

title: Neko's own voice cannot wake it
scenario: Detections while Neko is speaking (echo of its own voice).
expected: Ignored: no recording, no speech recognition call, no task.

title: No speech after the wake word: no recognition call
scenario: Wake word, then 5.3 s of silence.
expected: Back to listening after 5 s; speech recognition never called (nothing recorded is sent anywhere).

title: Speech recognition down is reported, listening resumes
scenario: The local speech service fails.
expected: No task; outcome reports the failure; state wake_listening.

title: A command is cut at 12 s
scenario: 15 s of continuous speech after the wake word.
expected: Recognition receives at most 12 s + 2 s pre-roll; one task.

title: Detector crash restarts it
scenario: The keyword detector raises (as N.E.K.O's does on WAKE_WORD_TIMEOUT).
expected: One error counted, detector restarted, back to wake_listening.

title: Paused microphone is ignored; resume works
scenario: Paused (POST /pause) during a full wake + command; then resumed.
expected: Nothing submitted while paused (status says paused); after resume the next command is submitted.

title: Two cancels from the screen are one cancel
scenario: POST /cancel twice while a command is being recorded.
expected: One cancellation, no task, back to listening.

title: A second wake word during a command does not double the task
scenario: The detector fires again while the command is recorded.
expected: Exactly one task.

title: Status never shows what was said
scenario: A command with private words.
expected: The status JSON (served to the Neko icon) contains none of the words.

title: 44.1 kHz microphones are resampled to 16 kHz
scenario: 1 s of 44.1 kHz audio.

title: State machine keeps up with real time
scenario: Per-frame processing time of the loop (fakes for detector/VAD).
expected: Under 5 ms per 40 ms frame.

title: Status server: loopback only, foreign web pages refused
scenario: The status/control server is asked from loopback and with a foreign Origin.
expected: Loopback answered; foreign origins refused (no web page can cancel or pause).

title: A long sentence starting with 'stop' is a task when nothing runs
scenario: 'stop the music and open notepad' with no task running.
expected: Submitted as a task, not swallowed as a cancel.

title: Wake recall at 0.5 m, owner's voice
scenario: 10 x 'Hey Neko' by the owner at 0.5 m (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Wake recall at 1.5 m, owner's voice
scenario: 10 x 'Hey Neko' at 1.5 m (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: False wakes in a normal room
scenario: hours of ambient audio and TV (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Cancel by voice, real microphone
scenario: owner says 'cancel' after the wake word (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Barge-in while Neko speaks
scenario: owner interrupts Neko's speech (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: No self-wake from the speakers
scenario: Neko's TTS through speakers into the microphone (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Speech recognition word error rate, owner
scenario: owner's real commands in English and Telugu (physical hardware).
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Short commands that start with a cancel word are tasks
scenario: Synthetic frames, fake detector/VAD; fake ASR returns 'cancel my meeting', 'stop the music', 'cancel my dentist appointment tomorrow' (nothing running), and the bare phrases 'cancel', 'Never mind.', 'nevermind', 'Forget it!', 'no thanks', 'quiet'. Guards against Neko silently dropping a real request.
expected: The three object commands are submitted as tasks; the six bare phrases cancel (no task).

title: Speech heard but no words recognised
scenario: Wake word, 1 s of speech, silence; the fake ASR returns an empty transcript (noise, a cough).
expected: Nothing submitted; outcome 'no words recognized'; no_speech counted; back to wake_listening.

title: Main agent refuses or is down: the voice outcome says so
scenario: The real submit_task() posts to a FAKE local widget that answers 409 'a task is already running'; then to an address where nothing listens.
expected: Both: outcome 'the main agent refused the task' with the reason ('already running' / 'URLError'), tasks_started 0, one error counted, back to listening; the widget received exactly {task: 'open notepad', mode: 'work'}.

title: Speech-recognition client: WAV out, text in, failure reported
scenario: The real transcribe() against a FAKE local speech server: 0.5 s of PCM; the server answers '  open notepad \n'; then the server answers 500 inside a full wake/command round.
expected: Text 'open notepad' (trimmed); the server received audio/wav, 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit, 8000 frames, language=en. On 500: outcome 'speech recognition failed', nothing submitted, back to listening.

title: 'Hey Neko, stop' reports whether the stop worked
scenario: Fake ASR says 'stop'; the real task_running()/stop_task() talk to a FAKE widget that shows a task in 'planning' and then answers the stop with ok=false 'nothing to stop'.
expected: The widget receives {action: 'stop'} once; the outcome is 'stop the running task' with ok=false and the note 'nothing to stop' (not a claimed stop); nothing submitted.

title: Command gain from the wake word: raise, never cut, never wrap
scenario: Synthetic levels: a quiet speaker (wake and command at 16), a loud one (20000), and a quiet wake word (100) followed by a loud command (10000).
expected: Command peak 256 (16x, the +24 dB cap); 20000 (1x, never reduced); 32767 with no negative values (clipped, not wrapped around); each submits once.

title: Status shows a muted microphone
scenario: One second of digital silence, then one second at full scale.
expected: Status audio: about -120 dBFS for the silent second (<= -100), about 0 dBFS for the loud one (>= -1); max and min kept.

title: The command ends one second after the speaker stops
scenario: Wake word, 2.0 s of speech, 3 s of silence (fake VAD: any non-zero sample is speech).
expected: One recognition call with 3.0-3.2 s of audio (2.0 s of speech + the 1 s end-of-command silence, to frame accuracy).

title: A slow starter is still heard
scenario: Wake word, then 4.5 s of silence, then 1 s of speech and 1.2 s of silence (the wait for speech is 5 s).
expected: The command is submitted once; its audio covers the pause and the speech (>= 5.5 s); no 'no speech' outcome.

title: Listening for hours does not grow memory
scenario: Two minutes of audio frames with no wake word (fake detector never fires).
expected: The pre-roll ring holds at most 2 s (+ one 40 ms frame); no command audio is kept; recognition never called.

title: Status server: DNS rebinding and other localhost pages refused
scenario: Real status server on a free port: GET /status and POST /pause with a non-loopback Host header; POST /pause and /resume from the widget's origins (localhost:48940, 127.0.0.1:48940); POST /resume from http://localhost:9999.
expected: 403, 403, 200, 403, 200 in that order; the foreign page could not resume the paused microphone; the widget could.

title: Recorded test audio is normalised like the microphone
scenario: A 1 s 48 kHz stereo WAV whose channels are opposite (L = -R); an 8-bit WAV; FileSource over 1 s of PCM.
expected: 16000 mono samples (+/-2) with the channels averaged (peak <= 50); the 8-bit file refused with ValueError; FileSource yields 100 whole 40 ms frames ending in 3 s of silence.

title: Microphone that only offers 44.1 kHz (real device)
scenario: On the laptop, a USB microphone whose driver refuses 16 kHz: MicSource must fall back to the device rate and resample, and a full 'Hey Neko, open notepad' must work. Needs the physical microphone; never simulated here.
expected: Measured on the laptop; DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.

title: Pause from the Neko icon with the real microphone
scenario: With the real microphone open, the owner pauses listening from the Neko icon, speaks 'Hey Neko' three times, then resumes. Needs the physical microphone; never simulated here.
expected: No detection while paused; detections resume after resume. DEFERRED — OWNER HARDWARE REQUIRED.
